description: GRAL is a Lagrangian atmospheric-dispersion model developed from work at Graz University of Technology and the Styrian provincial government. It tracks simulated particles through a three-dimensional wind field and can use an internal flow model for buildings and small terrain features. It can also link to the separate GRAMM wind-field model where topography matters. Inputs include emissions, meteorology, terrain and built geometry; outputs are modelled transport and pollutant concentration fields. Geography is the user-defined local site, while grid, meteorological period and output resolution depend on the setup, not a single fixed map. The calculation core and graphical interface are published under GPL-3.0, and the README points to a manual and an official validated release. The GitHub source and instructions are free to access. The README describes validation datasets, but this review did not assess their transferability to a new street canyon or industrial facility. GRAL serves road-traffic, pipeline and industrial emission-exposure simulations. The catalogue's model-aloha-chemical-dispersion is a separate release-dispersion model for comparison; no coupling was tested. No executable or dataset was downloaded.
inputs: Emission sources, meteorology, terrain and buildings
